Katie (CS): Hey team — quick checkin for Pelmor week0. Customer blocked on KMS access from their priv VPC, ECG flagged a renewal risk if we slip >2 weeks :concerned:
Ajay (Eng-Infra): Noted. Do we have their VPC endpoint details?
Katie (CS): They shared: VPC a-0a1b2c3d, subnets 10.10.0.0/24,10.10.1.0/24. They think egress is allowed but KMS calls fail with 403.
Sam SRE: 403 usually IAM or endpoint policy. Can you paste the kms error snippet from the app logs?
Katie (CS): sure — paste from their agent:
```
2026-03-19T14:10:02Z ERROR api.Request KMSAccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/pelmor-app-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
```
Maria (SE): That looks like key policy or the role missing kms:Decrypt. Also if they use a VPC endpoint, the endpoint policy can block KMS. Pelmor mentioned a restrictive endpoint policy.
Ajay (Eng-Infra): Can they run this test from inside the VPC?
Katie (CS): they ran curl from an EC2 in the subnet, got connection OK to kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com:443 but API returns 403.
Sam SRE: OK so network path is valid. Two leads: 1) IAM role lacks kms permissions; 2) KMS key policy denies the principal or requires aws:sourceVpc condition.
Maria (SE): Action: Maria will draft minimal policy to attach to the key and role so we can isolate. I'll post snippet here.
Maria (SE): policy snippets — role inline policy (attach to pelmor-app-role):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01"
    }
  ]
}
```
Maria (SE): And a permissive key policy to allow the aws account's roles for now:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowAccountRoles",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```
Ajay (Eng-Infra): If they have a security audit requirement we shouldn't keep this permissive. For debug it's ok for a short window. We should add an egress rule reminder: the VPC endpoint policy should allow kms:Decrypt for the principal or the aws:SourceVpc?
Katie (CS): They do have strict audit; suggested we coordinate a temporary exception w/ their security team. This ties to renewal risk — CS flagged that delayed onboarding >14 days increases churn probability.
Sam SRE: Proposed runbook: 1) Apply role policy + permissive key policy (SE), 2) Confirm call succeeds (Customer), 3) Lock key policy to specific role and add aws:SourceVpc condition (Infra), 4) Document in onboard runbook.
Maria (SE): I'll post the exact commands for step 1.
Maria (SE): command to test from inside VPC:
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://cipher.blob --region us-west-2 --profile pelmor-test
```
Katie (CS): Customer timezone: PST. Can we have step 1 done by EOD PST tomorrow? They want a live debug session then.
Ajay (Eng-Infra): I can make the policy change tonight but will coordinate with security for the temporary window.
Sam SRE: I'll standby to review CloudTrail entries for KMS calls and verify audit log capture.
DeployBot: deploy request queued — change set for key policy prepared by Maria, awaiting Ajay approval.
Katie (CS): Great. One more ask from customer: they want audit log retention set to 1 year and forwarded to their SIEM. Is that on our enablement scope?
Maria (SE): We can add a quick doc and a sample CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to Kinesis Firehose to their SIEM. I'll draft and attach to the runbook.
Katie (CS): OK team — owners: Maria (policy + docs), Ajay (apply + security approvals), Sam (audit verification). I'll update the CS risk tracker: set renewal_risk = elevated until onboarding completes.
Ajay (Eng-Infra): noted. I'll ping when change is live.
Katie (CS): Thanks all :thumbsup:
